plan.estimand: Omnibus F-test power under one-way fixed-effects ANOVA
plan.hypothesis: H0: All k=3 group means are equal vs. H1: At least one group mean differs, indexed by population eta-squared η² = 0.08
assumptions: Independent observations within and between groups
Population eta-squared η² = 0.08 specifies the true noncentrality parameter
scientific_notes: Eta-squared η² = (SS_between) / (SS_total) is the population effect size
Under the null hypothesis (η² = 0), the F-statistic follows F(k-1, N-k) = F(2, 72)
Under the alternative (η² = 0.08), the noncentrality parameter λ relates to η² through: λ = [η² / (1 - η²)] × (N - k) = [0.08 / 0.92] × 72 ≈ 6.26
The F-statistic under H1 follows a noncentral F distribution: F'(k-1, N-k, λ)
This is a fixed-effects ANOVA; R pwr::pwr.f2.test or scipy.stats for noncentral F calculation
Omnibus test is inherently two-tailed in interpretation (any departure from equality of means)

# One-way ANOVA power calculation
# Design: balanced, 3 groups, N=75 total (25 per group)
# Population eta-squared = 0.08, alpha = 0.05

# Parameters
k <- 3  # number of groups
N <- 75  # total sample size
n_per_group <- N / k  # 25 per group
eta_sq <- 0.08  # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate noncentrality parameter lambda
# For one-way ANOVA: lambda = [eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq)] * (N - k)
lambda <- (eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq)) * (N - k)

# Degrees of freedom
df1 <- k - 1  # numerator df (between groups)
df2 <- N - k  # denominator df (within groups)

# Critical F-value at alpha = 0.05
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)

# Power = P(F > f_crit | noncentral F with lambda)
# Using the noncentral F cumulative distribution function
power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)

cat("One-Way ANOVA Power Calculation\n")
cat("================================\n\n")
cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Number of groups (k): %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size (N): %d\n", N))
cat(sprintf("  Sample size per group: %d\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Population eta-squared (η²): %.4f\n", eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (α): %.4f\n\n", alpha))

cat("Degrees of Freedom:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Numerator (between): %d\n", df1))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator (within): %d\n\n", df2))

cat("Noncentrality Parameter:\n")
cat(sprintf("  λ = [η² / (1 - η²)] × (N - k)\n"))
cat(sprintf("  λ = [%.4f / %.4f] × %d\n", eta_sq, 1 - eta_sq, N - k))
cat(sprintf("  λ = %.6f\n\n", lambda))

cat("Critical Value and Power:\n")
cat(sprintf("  F-critical at α = 0.05: %.6f\n", f_crit))
cat(sprintf("  Power (1 - β): %.6f\n\n", power))

# Output for JSON
result <- list(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)

# Also include supporting calculations
cat("Supporting Details:\n")
cat(sprintf("  F(%.0f, %.0f) critical value: %.6f\n", df1, df2, f_crit))
cat(sprintf("  Noncentral F'(%.0f, %.0f, λ=%.6f) power: %.6f\n\n", df1, df2, lambda, power))

# JSON output
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(result)),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)
cat(POWER_AGENT_RESULT)

# Carefully derive the correct noncentrality parameter
# This requires understanding the relationship between eta² and the noncentrality λ
# used in the noncentral F distribution

# From statistical theory:
# Under H1, the F-statistic follows F'(df1, df2, λ) where
# λ = (MS_between / σ²) × df1
#   = (SS_between / (k-1)) / σ² × (k-1)
#   = SS_between / σ²

# Also, η² = SS_between / SS_total = SS_between / (SS_between + SS_within)
# And: MS_within (pooled) = σ² (unbiased estimator)

# Under the alternative:
# SS_between = λ × σ² (relating the noncentrality to sum of squares)
# SS_total = SS_between + SS_within
# MS_within ~ σ²

# The noncentrality in the noncentral F is:
# λ = Σ nᵢ (μᵢ - μ̄)² / σ²  (sum across groups)

# For balanced design with equal group means deviations:
# If we parameterize by η² directly, we need to invert:
# η² = SS_between / SS_total
# Under H1 with effect, this constrains the mean structure

# Actually, let me use the RELATIONSHIP from standard references:
# For one-way ANOVA with effect size f (Cohen's f):
# f² = Σ(μᵢ - μ̄)² / σ²  (variance of group means relative to error variance)
# NOT per-group; this is the TOTAL effect

# For balanced design: Σ(μᵢ - μ̄)² = n × Σ(μᵢ - μ̄)²  [per-group deviations squared]
# So: f² = n × Σ(μᵢ - μ̄)² / σ²

# The noncentrality λ for the NONCENTRAL F distribution is:
# λ = n × f² × (k) [One parameterization]
# OR
# λ = Σ nᵢ(μᵢ - μ̄)² / σ² = (N - k) × f² × (k) / (?)

# Let me check empirically what pwr.anova.test is computing

k <- 3
N <- 75
n_per_group <- N / k
eta_sq <- 0.08
f_squared <- eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq)
f_effect <- sqrt(f_squared)
alpha <- 0.05

cat("Reconciling the noncentrality parameter\n")

# For noncentral F'(v₁, v₂, λ) in ANOVA:
# λ² = n × Σ(μᵢ - μ̄)² / σ² = n × f² × k  [for balanced]

df2 <- N - k

            power_lambda_cohen_book, ifelse(abs(power_pwr - power_lambda_cohen_book) < 1e-10, "YES", "NO")))

# One-way ANOVA power calculation
# Design: balanced, 3 groups, N=75 total (25 per group)
# Population eta-squared = 0.08, alpha = 0.05

# Parameters
k <- 3  # number of groups
N <- 75  # total sample size
n_per_group <- N / k  # 25 per group
eta_sq <- 0.08  # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate noncentrality parameter lambda
# For one-way ANOVA: lambda = [eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq)] * (N - k)
lambda <- (eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq)) * (N - k)

# Degrees of freedom
df1 <- k - 1  # numerator df (between groups)
df2 <- N - k  # denominator df (within groups)

# Critical F-value at alpha = 0.05
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)

# Power = P(F > f_crit | noncentral F with lambda)
# Using the noncentral F cumulative distribution function
power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
